Narrative: Roustabout observed working on the monkey board at 8 meters height without secondary lanyard attached during casing running operation. Wind gusts of 25 knots recorded; 100% tie-off was not maintained while transitioning between pipe fingers.

Contractor technician bypassed lockout/tagout mechanical interlock on high-pressure test manifold (3200 psi). Line was not depressurized before flange unbolting and no isolation certificate was affixed to the ESD valve.

Fixed sensor detected 16 ppm H2S release during tripping out of hole near the shale shaker pit. Two mud technicians were working without personal gas monitors and without emergency escape breathing apparatus staged within arm reach.

Contract welder attempted hot work grinding on live crude oil storage tank #9 roof nozzle without a hot work permit and without an explosive gas check. LEL monitor was not present within the 15-meter hot zone.

Crane was lifting a suspended load of drill collars over an occupied walkway without an established exclusion zone. Tag lines were not used to control load rotation and no dedicated banksman was posted.
Field crew entered the mud pit for cleaning without a confined space entry permit or prior atmospheric testing. No standby attendant was posted at the entry point and rescue equipment was not staged.
Worker was positioned directly in the line of fire while unspooling wireline under tension near the wellhead. No exclusion barrier tape was set up around the tensioned line path.
Hand tool dropped from an elevated platform during pipe rack maintenance; no injury occurred. Toe-board and edge protection were not installed along the platform's open edge.
Fire extinguisher inspection tag at the rig floor was found expired by four months. No immediate hazard was present but statutory compliance signage near the mud pumps was also missing.
Operator observed walking across an active pipe rack without using the designated crossover platform, stepping directly over a pressurized flowline instead of the marked walkway.
